current_mapping.description: describe characteristics, significance, and generation of programming languages;

stem: Which of the following generation of computers uses modern programming languages like Python and Java?
explanation: Fourth-generation computers (1971–present) use VLSI microprocessors and modern high-level / object-oriented and scripting programming languages such as Python, Java, C++, and SQL.

option_feedback.reason: First-generation computers used vacuum tubes and were programmed in binary machine language (1GL).
Second-generation computers used transistors and assembly/early procedural languages like FORTRAN and COBOL.
Third-generation computers used integrated circuits (ICs) and structured procedural languages like C, Pascal, and BASIC.

stem: Examples of volatile memory are
explanation: Both Random Access Memory (RAM) and CPU Cache memory are semiconductor volatile memories that lose all stored data immediately when electrical power is switched off.

option_feedback.reason: A Compact Disc (CD) is a non-volatile optical secondary storage medium.
Both a hard disk drive (magnetic) and a CD (optical) are non-volatile secondary storage devices.
A hard disk drive is a non-volatile magnetic storage device that retains data without power.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a pointing device?
explanation: A barcode reader is an optical scanning input device that reads printed vertical bars (Universal Product Codes) using a laser beam, rather than controlling a screen cursor/pointer.

option_feedback.reason: A mouse is the most common pointing device used to move the on-screen cursor.
A light pen is a light-sensitive pointing device used to select items or draw directly on a screen.
A joystick is a lever-based pointing device used to control cursor/object movement in games and simulations.

stem:

• Introduced in 1960s
• Executes billions of instructions per second
• Used in the organisations that has hundreds of users
The type of digital computer that has the given properties is
explanation: Minicomputers (mid-range servers) were introduced in the mid-1960s (such as the DEC PDP series) to serve medium-sized organisations with dozens to hundreds of concurrent terminal users.

option_feedback.reason: Supercomputers are built for scientific/weather simulations executing trillions of FLOPS rather than mid-sized organisational multi-user administration.
Microcomputers (personal computers) were introduced in the 1970s for single individual users.
Mainframe computers were introduced in the 1950s (e.g., UNIVAC/IBM 700 series) to serve thousands of enterprise users.

• Faster than other levels of cache memory.
• Present inside the microprocessor.

I. Level 1
II. Level 2
III. Level 3
explanation: Level 1 (L1) cache (I only) is built directly into the microprocessor core and operates at the CPU's clock speed, making it the fastest of all cache memory levels.

option_feedback.reason: Level 3 (L3) cache is the largest and slowest of the three cache levels.
Level 2 (L2) cache is slower than Level 1 (L1) cache, so only I satisfies 'faster than other levels of cache memory'.
Both Level 2 and Level 3 cache are slower than Level 1 cache.

explanation: Running an online social media marketing campaign requires capturing product photos/promotional videos (camera) and designing, typing, and uploading posts online (mouse and keyboard).

options.A: It allows a user to install programs.
options.B: It allows a user to create new users.
options.C: It allows a user to run pre-installed programs.
options.D: It allows a user to login without username and password.

explanation: The user management subsystem of an operating system enables an administrator to create and manage new user accounts, assign passwords, and configure access privileges.

Running programs falls under process execution/management rather than user management.

explanation: Based on the number of concurrent users supported, operating systems are classified into two main categories: Single-user operating systems and Multi-user operating systems (or by tasking/processing mode).

stem: A type of an operating system that is used in oil refinery for indicating that temperature is getting too high is
explanation: An oil refinery temperature monitoring and safety alarm system requires immediate, deterministic response within strict time deadlines, which is provided by a Real-Time Operating System (RTOS).

option_feedback.reason: A multi-user system focuses on allowing multiple users to share a central computer rather than guaranteed millisecond hazard response.
A time-sharing system slices CPU time among interactive users and can experience scheduling delays.
A batch processing system queues jobs for later offline execution and cannot respond instantly to live emergencies.

I. Spell check of words
II. Inserting pictures and tables
III. Changing the page orientation
IV. Data filtering and visualisation
explanation: A word processor (such as MS Word) provides spell checking (I), inserting pictures and tables (II), and changing page orientation between Portrait and Landscape (III), whereas data filtering and chart visualisation (IV) are primary features of spreadsheet/data analysis software (such as MS Excel).

option_feedback.reason: Statement IV (data filtering and visualisation) is a spreadsheet feature, not a core word processor feature.
Includes IV (spreadsheet data filtering) and omits I and III.
Includes IV (spreadsheet data filtering) and omits I (spell check).

stem: The shortcut key used to move the cursor at the top of the document is
explanation: In Microsoft Word, pressing Ctrl + Home moves the insertion point (cursor) directly to the very beginning (top) of the entire document.

option_feedback.reason: Pressing Home alone moves the cursor only to the beginning of the current line.
Pressing Page Up scrolls the view up by one screenful rather than jumping to the top of the document.
Pressing Ctrl + Page Up moves the cursor to the top of the previous page.

stem: The MOST suitable page orientation for making a certificate is
explanation: Certificates are traditionally printed wider than they are tall, which uses the Landscape (horizontal) page orientation.

option_feedback.reason: Legal is a paper size (8.5 × 14 inches), not a page orientation.
Letter is a paper size (8.5 × 11 inches), not a page orientation.
Portrait is a vertical orientation (taller than wide) used for letters and reports rather than wide certificates.

stem: Which of the following tabs contain the options for setting the line spacing of a document?
explanation: In Microsoft Word, paragraph spacing (Before/After) and line spacing options are available in the Paragraph group on the Layout (Page Layout) tab (as well as the Home tab; the 2023 AKU-EB official key credits D: Layout).

option_feedback.reason: While line spacing also appears on the Home tab ribbon, the official AKU-EB 2023 key under SLO 3.1.3/3.1.7 (Page Layout) specifies D (Layout).
The Insert tab is used to add tables, pictures, headers, and footers.
The Design tab is used for document themes, watermarks, and page borders.

explanation: Baud Rate = Bit Rate / Bits per signal unit = 2000 bps / 2 bits per baud = 1000 baud.

explanation: 1 Mebibyte (1 MiB) = 2^20 bytes = 1024 KiB = 1024 × 1024 bytes = 1,048,576 bytes.

stem: An artificial satellite is precisely positioned in the space with an orbit speed that

options.A: is more than the rotational speed of the Earth.
options.B: is more than the rotational speed of the Moon.
options.C: matches with the rotational speed of the Earth.
options.D: matches with the rotational speed of the Moon.

explanation: A geostationary communication satellite orbits above the equator at an angular speed that exactly matches the rotational speed of the Earth (24-hour period), so it appears stationary relative to ground antennas.

option_feedback.reason: If its orbital angular speed exceeded Earth's rotation, the satellite would drift ahead of fixed ground dishes.
Communication satellites are synchronised with the Earth's rotation, not the Moon's.

current_mapping.description: describe transmission impairments (attenuation, distortion, and noise/crosstalk) and communication performance metrics (bandwidth, data rate, baud rate, and SNR);

stem: If the strength of a signal falls off when the distance increases, then the type of transmission impairment will be
explanation: Attenuation is the gradual loss or weakening of signal strength (amplitude) as it travels over increasing distances through a transmission medium due to resistance and dispersion.

option_feedback.reason: Crosstalk is electromagnetic interference coupling from one adjacent wire into another.
Distortion is the alteration of a composite signal's waveform shape when different frequencies travel at different speeds.
Amplification is the boosting of signal strength using an amplifier or repeater, not an impairment.

current_mapping.description: describe the functions of network communication devices (Modem, NIC, Switch, Router, Gateway, Access Point);

stem: Which of the following communication devices is the BEST alternative of a hub?
explanation: A network switch is an intelligent multi-port LAN device that replaces a passive hub by inspecting MAC addresses and forwarding frames only to the intended destination port instead of broadcasting to all ports.

option_feedback.reason: A router connects different IP networks (e.g., LAN to WAN) rather than serving as a direct multi-port LAN hub replacement.
A dial-up modem converts digital data to analog audio over telephone lines.
A Network Interface Card (NIC) is an adapter inside a single computer rather than a central multi-port LAN concentrator.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between asynchronous and synchronous data transmission modes;

stem: The type of transmission in which start/ stop bits are used is
explanation: Asynchronous transmission sends data character by character (byte by byte) framed by a leading Start bit ('0') and a trailing Stop bit ('1') to synchronise the receiver for each byte.

option_feedback.reason: Satellite transmission refers to an unguided wireless medium, not character-framing synchronisation.
Microwave transmission refers to an unguided line-of-sight wireless medium.
Synchronous transmission sends continuous blocks/frames of data synchronised by a shared clock timing signal without per-byte start/stop bits.

stem: Radio broadcasting and transmission of data from a computer to a printer are examples of
explanation: Both radio broadcasting (station to listener) and standard computer-to-printer data transmission are unidirectional (one-way only) communication channels, which are examples of simplex transmission.

option_feedback.reason: Full-duplex transmission sends data simultaneously in both directions (like a telephone call).
Radio broadcasting is one-way simplex, not two-way half-duplex.
Neither radio broadcasting nor computer-to-printer data flow is half-duplex or full-duplex.

stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE about client/ server networks?

options.A: It does not provide centralised security.
options.B: It can be expanded up to thousands of computers.
options.C: It is generally used for long distance communication.
options.D: These networks are considered as wide area networks.

explanation: Statement A is FALSE because a primary advantage of a client/server network is that dedicated central servers enforce strong centralised security, user authentication, and access control.

option_feedback.reason: Client/server networks are highly scalable and can expand to support thousands of clients.

II. It allows software sharing.
III. It allows file management.

explanation: Computer networks allow multiple connected users to share a single internet connection (I) and share networked software applications/licences from a server (II), whereas file management (III) and memory management (IV) are functions of an Operating System.

option_feedback.reason: Statement III (file management) is an operating system function rather than a computer network function.

explanation: A network operated by a telephone or cable company covering an entire city to provide DSL broadband to urban subscribers is a Metropolitan Area Network (MAN).

option_feedback.reason: A LAN is restricted to a single room, office floor, or building.
A WAN spans multiple countries or continents rather than a single city.
A PAN covers only a few metres around a single person's devices.

current_mapping.description: describe network topologies (bus, star, ring, mesh, tree, and hybrid) along with their advantages and disadvantages;

stem:
Consider the given properties.
• Every node is connected with other nodes.
• It is the most reliable network topology.
• It is the most expensive topology.
Based on the given properties, the network topology is identified as
explanation: In a full mesh topology, every node has a dedicated point-to-point cable link to every other node, making it the most fault-tolerant (reliable) and also the most expensive topology due to n(n - 1)/2 cables.

option_feedback.reason: Bus topology uses a single shared backbone cable and is the least expensive, least fault-tolerant topology.
Star topology connects nodes only to a central switch/hub, and fails if the central device fails.
Ring topology connects each node only to its two immediate neighbours in a loop.
